findings.text: the negative_control_note says the mutation leaves the first case green because it does not depend on the log, which is called the discrimination, but the red log it cites collected one case only ("1 failed in 2.81s", the failing-replay case) and the first case does read the log at tests/test_verify_gate_replay_is_diagnosable.py:249 through replay_log's assertion at :163 and asserts the log's header and its EXIT= line, so under the same mutation it would redden too — the claimed discrimination was never measured and, read against the source, does not hold, which leaves the negative control proving only that the second case is sensitive to the discard.

the baseline_suite line (and the after_suite line below it) are prose beginning with a log's path rather than the JSON the brief's manifest contract asks for at prompt.txt:131, so the review store's resolver returns the whole sentence and opens nothing, and every read of this review is annotated added_failure_count unmeasured; the true pair (0 added, no ids) is stored here only because it was derived by hand from the two logs.

the base arm's log names no revision — the line is empty and two git errors stand above it — because run-suite-arm.sh:11 computes it with git -C rev-parse inside a tree that git archive extracted and so is not a repository, against the brief's own requirement (prompt.txt:126) that a gate log's first line name the revision it ran at; the head arm names a9ce802d, so a reader of the base log alone cannot confirm which tree produced the two FAILED ids the whole node rests on.

gate_log_evidence.note: derived by hand from the two logs because the reviewed manifest names them as prose, so the read-time annotation reports the count unmeasured

item_verdicts.diff: a9ce802d is the rewrite, the log capture, the report and the finding fields; 3a9eec99 is the landing record and its figure only; the five removed lines are the replaced argv, the dropped capture_output and the finding's old return, all intentional and all accounted for in the commit bodies.
item_verdicts.done_when: the gate rehearses the reviewed node's own measure and both arms are logged — the base arm is red with exactly the two new cases failed ("2 failed, 72 passed", EXIT=1 at logs/baseline-suite.log), the head arm is green ("74 passed", EXIT=0 at logs/after-suite.log), and the two cases assert the report's log path (tests/test_verify_gate_replay_is_diagnosable.py:163), the replay running in the checkout rather than the removed worktree (:216) and a failing replay's ids and stderr in the log (:261).
item_verdicts.goal: both driving followups are met in production code and not only in the test — the replay reads the worktree roots the run's own release audit recorded (reckon/crew/promotion.py:1148), rewrites each to the --checkout-path it is replaying at, at path-segment boundaries and only when the candidate is not already the checkout (:1174, :1211), keeps its own stdout and stderr in a log beside the run (:824, :856), records that path on the report (:1402, :1418, :1504) and carries the failing ids into the merged finding (:1431) — and the premise holds on a real row, whose release.worktree_audit.worktrees[0].path is exactly the shape _recorded_worktree_roots consumes.
item_verdicts.manifest: the manifest names both commits, both arms' logs, the module each arm imported and the resolved cwd, the mutation and the red log; two of its fields are defective and are findings 1 and 2 below.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff b5c8ce92..3a9eec99 touches exactly the four declared paths and no fifth — reckon/crew/promotion.py (218 added, 5 removed), tests/test_verify_gate_replay_is_diagnosable.py (297/0), the landing fragment (100/0) and its figure (93/0) — with no plan meta, no state or index file, and no peer path, every hunk inside the declared set.

justifications.durability: the log carries a header naming the tree, the command and the module actually imported (reckon/crew/promotion.py:827) and the finding carries node ids rather than a pass/fail bit, but the log is rewritten whole at a fixed name per run, so a second replay of the same run silently replaces the log an earlier report still cites.
justifications.evidence: the two cases are red at base and green at head with both arms logged and the ids readable from the logs, but two pieces of the manifest's own evidence do not hold — the negative control's claimed discrimination (manifest line 29) is contradicted by the red log it cites and by tests/test_verify_gate_replay_is_diagnosable.py:249, and the base arm's log records no revision (logs/baseline-suite.log:4).
justifications.fit: the helpers sit beside the gate-replay code they serve and reuse the module's existing log writer, and the cases build a real repository and assert on the report, the log and the committed row, but the escaped-write check resolves the config home by a hardcoded path (tests/test_verify_gate_replay_is_diagnosable.py:89) while _config_home() reads RECKON_HOME first, so under the fixture's own monkeypatch that half of the assertion is vacuous.
justifications.goal_fidelity: both followups are met for the row shape they were written from, and the residual is the row that carries no release audit — _recorded_worktree_roots returns nothing for it (reckon/crew/promotion.py:1148), so such a run's replay still runs at the root its stored command pins, which is the not-run-versus-failed class the first followup names.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --numstat b5c8ce92..3a9eec99 lists four files and no fifth, each one named in the brief's declared write paths, with the landing commit touching only the evidence path it announced.
